attempts.reason_tested: confounder in SRC-F: anaemia, total leukocytes, neutrophils, illness days
attempts.method: Rank-based partial correlation (ranks residualised on covariate ranks by OLS, bootstrap 2000, t-test p) of monocyte count with dullness (4 - habitus_score) in B. rossi PCR-positive dogs, shared/tidy/DS05.features.json + DS05.outcomes.json; script experiments/SV-META/refutation/scripts/K01_checks.py, seed 20261112
attempts.result: Unadjusted rho +0.448 (p 1.3e-08, n 147). Partial on haematocrit +0.28 (+0.11 to +0.42, p 0.0006); on WBC +0.38 (p 2.9e-06); on segmented neutrophils +0.42; on band neutrophils +0.33 (p 5.6e-05); on illness days +0.45; on haematocrit + WBC +0.32 (p 9.5e-05); on haematocrit + segs + bands +0.26 (p 0.0016); on all five +0.29 (+0.13 to +0.44, p 0.0006, n 145); adding lymphocytes, platelets and temperature +0.28 (p 0.0009, n 141). Anaemia explains about a third of the association (haematocrit with dullness rho -0.53; monocytes with haematocrit -0.44), but it does not remove it.

attempts.reason_tested: general leukocytosis rather than monocytes (specificity, SRC-F)
attempts.method: Same file: other leukocyte counts with dullness, unadjusted and after partialling out the monocyte count; monocyte fraction of WBC
attempts.result: WBC rho +0.27, segs +0.19, lymphocytes +0.20, bands +0.38 with dullness. After partialling monocytes: WBC -0.04 (p 0.66), segs -0.06, lymphocytes +0.01, bands +0.20 (p 0.015). Monocyte fraction of WBC with dullness +0.33 (p 5.7e-05). In DS05 the monocyte count carries the leukocyte signal, not the other way round.

attempts.method: Drop the 3 E. canis co-infected dogs (monocytic ehrlichiosis could raise monocytes and dullness); drop the top 5% of monocyte counts; dichotomies of dullness (Cliff, permutation 10000)
attempts.result: Without E. canis: rho +0.453 (n 144). Without top 5% monocytes: +0.422 (n 139). Dull >= 2 vs < 2: Cliff +0.55 (+0.39 to +0.68), p 0.0001. Only 10 dogs were BAR, so 'any dullness' compares 137 with 10 (Cliff +0.38, p 0.039).

attempts.reason_tested: hard-outcome sources: effect not beyond total leukocytes; label partly contains leukocytes
attempts.method: S-CB517 (SRC-A, died vs survived, died includes euthanasia for poor prognosis) and S-CB017 day 1 (SRC-D, B. canis, complicated vs uncomplicated): Cliff delta of monocyte fraction of WBC and of WBC-rank-adjusted monocyte residuals; WBC and segs by outcome
attempts.result: SRC-A: monocyte count Cliff +0.25 (-0.18 to +0.63, p 0.17; medians 0.81 vs 0.52); WBC +0.22 (p 0.23); monocyte fraction +0.11 (-0.28 to +0.46, p 0.53); WBC-adjusted +0.19 (p 0.30). SRC-D: monocyte count +0.23 (p 0.24), WBC +0.23, monocyte % -0.01 (-0.41 to +0.38, p 0.96), WBC-adjusted +0.17 (p 0.43). The SRC-D 'complicated' label requires SIRS, of which WBC is a criterion. In both sources with a hard or clinical outcome the monocyte difference is no larger than the total-leukocyte difference, and neither interval excludes 0.

attempts.reason_tested: contradiction: CB504 fewer P-selectin-positive monocytes in non-survivors
attempts.method: Read /core/articles/CB504_2015_platelet-activation-platelet-leukocyte-interaction-naturally.md and the abstract-only text /core/data/markdown/CB504.md (source_format abstract)
attempts.result: CB504 (DOI 10.1016/j.tvjl.2015.05.008): CD62P-positive monocytes 58.9% in 29 survivors, 39.2% in 7 non-survivors (no significant difference), survivors above controls (35.3%) and non-survivors not. Same cohort as SRC-A (CH03, Onderstepoort Oct 2011 - Apr 2013), so probably overlapping dogs. The marker is platelet-monocyte aggregation, not monocyte number, and the comparison is underpowered, so it does not reject a count claim. It does contradict the word 'activation': the one direct cellular activation marker measured in B. rossi points the other way in non-survivors, as do monocyte activation markers in Malawian children with severe malaria (10.1111/pim.12319).

attempts.reason_tested: construct validity: monocyte count, MCP-1 and serum CD14 are not one measure
attempts.method: Spearman of monocyte count with MCP-1 among infected dogs in S-CB517 (SRC-A) and S-CB017 day 1 (SRC-D); CB517 full text (/core/data/markdown/CB517.md) discussion
attempts.result: SRC-A rho -0.17 (p 0.09, n 97); SRC-D +0.20 (p 0.28, n 31). CB517 itself remarks on the absence of monocytosis despite high MCP-1. The theme combines a circulating count, a chemokine and a serum receptor protein that do not co-vary, so the combined Z supports 'several monocyte-lineage indicators lean the same way', not one 'activation' process.

attempts.reason_tested: assay/sample artefact: DS07 CD14 confounded with haemoglobin beta (haemolysis)
attempts.method: shared/tidy/DS07.features.json + DS07.outcomes.json (opened by this check; not previously opened by SV-META), infected dogs: Spearman CD14 (A0A1S7J0A8) with haemoglobin beta (P60524); Cliff of CD14 rank residuals after HBB ranks; rank partial correlation; plex-median-centred CD14
attempts.result: CD14 vs HBB rho +0.46 (p 0.008, n 32; within complicated +0.58, within uncomplicated +0.13). CD14 complicated vs uncomplicated: unadjusted Cliff +0.42 (+0.04 to +0.75, p 0.044); HBB-adjusted +0.24 (-0.18 to +0.63, p 0.27); partial r +0.22 (p 0.25); plex-centred +0.39 (p 0.062). HBB itself +0.48 (p 0.022), and the label contains haematocrit < 0.15. About half the CD14 signal goes with the haemoglobin signal; in-vivo haemolysis, anaemia severity and stored-sample haemolysis cannot be separated. Replacing SRC-C with the adjusted value: 4-source Z 3.60 (p 0.00016); without SRC-F Z 1.91 (p 0.028).

attempts.method: /experiments/SV-07/report.md sections 4.1-4.5 and the summary table; cohort fields of the CB517, CB504, CB112 notes
attempts.result: T02 uses S-CB517 (S-CB050 cohort 1, 2011-2013) for SRC-A. The unverified DS07 overlap runs through DS04 to S-CB050 cohort 2 (2014; cases 126, 127, 131), which are not S-CB517 dogs. SRC-B are experimental Beagles, SRC-F is an Eastern Cape clinic in 2021, SRC-D is Zagreb. No dog is counted twice among the T02 indicators. CB504 (not an indicator) is probably the same dogs as SRC-A.

attempts.reason_tested: post hoc choice of monocyte count over MCP-1
attempts.method: Recomputed equal-weight one-sided Stouffer for every choice of marker (count or MCP-1) in SRC-A and SRC-B, with and without SRC-F (indicator p values from out/themes.csv)
attempts.result: With SRC-F: Z 3.94 (count, count) to 4.80 (MCP-1, MCP-1). Without SRC-F: Z 2.31 to 3.29. The count is the most conservative choice, so the choice did not inflate the result.

attempts.reason_tested: correction for themes; dependence on the hypothesis-generating source
attempts.method: Leave-out combinations (K01_checks.py, 'combinations'); themes.csv notes ('themes chosen after the results were seen'; 'monocytes with habitus already seen (EXP01)')
attempts.result: SRC-F generated the idea (EXP01) and carries the combination; its p is a permutation floor (1e-4; analytic p 1.3e-08). Without SRC-F: Z 2.31, p 0.0105, Bonferroni over 8 themes 0.084. Without SRC-F and SRC-C (the CB112 positive control): Z 1.56, p 0.060. Monocyte count alone in sources other than SRC-F (A, B): Z 1.56, p 0.060. The spec screen (BH q 0.00016, every leave-one-out p < 0.05) is met, but the replication evidence outside the source that suggested it does not survive the theme correction.

attempts.reason_tested: already published in a CB article
attempts.method: Grep of /core/articles/CB*.md and /core/data/markdown/CB*.md for monocyte, MCP-1/CCL2 and CD14 with severity terms; read CB107, CB517, CB037, CB017, CB112, CB119, CB147, CB126, CB098 notes and relevant passages
attempts.result: MCP-1 with severity is published in B. rossi by CB517 (non-survivors, 10.1371/journal.pone.0150113) and CB037 (critically ill and non-survivors, independent cohort), and in B. canis by CB017 (complicated, 10.1371/journal.pone.0190474). CB112 (10.1038/s41598-023-37312-9) reports higher CD14 in complicated dogs. CB107 (2023 review) combines the B. rossi and B. canis CCL2 findings and states that they indicate classical monocyte activation in severe canine babesiosis. CB119, CB129 and CB147 describe monocyte-macrophage expansion in tissues of fatal B. rossi cases. The cross-source CCL2 form of the claim (T02s) is therefore already published. The circulating-monocyte-count form is not: CB517 reported no monocyte difference by outcome, CB126 (the DS05 article) did not relate monocytes to habitus, and CB098 reports monocyte differences by dose, not by severity.

attempts.reason_tested: marker in the severity label; weak sources
attempts.method: Outcome definitions in the tidy outcomes files; SRC-B design (DS02 features)
attempts.result: DS05 habitus does not contain any leukocyte value. The DS07 label contains band neutrophils and haematocrit, not CD14. The S-CB017 label contains SIRS (WBC), which partly contains monocyte count (see the hard-outcome attempt). SRC-B compares dose (3 vs 2 Beagles, minimum exact two-sided p 0.2), not severity, but it gets equal weight in the Stouffer combination.

verdict_reason: No single check rejects the lead. The DS05 monocyte-dullness association survives adjustment for haematocrit, total and differential leukocytes and illness days (partial rho about +0.28), and the post hoc marker choice was conservative. But the cross-source support outside the source that suggested it is weak: without SRC-F, Z 2.31, Bonferroni over 8 themes 0.084. In the two hard-outcome sources the monocyte difference is no larger than the WBC difference, and half of the DS07 CD14 signal goes with haemoglobin beta. Monocyte count does not track MCP-1, the CCL2 form is already published (CB107, CB517, CB037, CB017), and the only direct activation marker in B. rossi (CB504) points the other way in non-survivors.

human_counterpart.claim: Sepsis: plasma MCP-1 correlated best with organ dysfunction and was the only cytokine independently associated with mortality
Sepsis meta-analysis (10 studies, 1617 patients): presepsin (sCD14-ST) higher in non-survivors, pooled SMD 0.92
Falciparum malaria, Mozambican adults: soluble CD14 (monocyte/macrophage activation marker) correlated with disease severity
Complicated falciparum malaria: serum sCD14 raised and higher with renal failure, but not related to parasitaemia, fever or clearance times
Malawian children: monocyte activation and adhesion markers (HLA-DR, CD86, CD11b) and cytokine-producing monocytes lower in cerebral malaria and severe malarial anaemia than in controls
Malaysian Borneo: MCP-1 lower in complicated than uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria (small groups), higher in complicated P. knowlesi

canine_parallel_already_made: Partly yes. For CCL2 (MCP-1) and monocyte activation, CB107 (review) synthesises CB517 and CB017. CB037, CB517 and CB017 are primary MCP-1 severity findings, CB112 is the CD14 finding, and CB119, CB129 and CB147 describe tissue monocyte-macrophage expansion in fatal B. rossi. No CB article makes the claim for the circulating monocyte count across sources, and CB517 reported no monocyte difference by outcome.
